faqLeft.q: What engine does the Land Rover Defender D300 use?
faqLeft.a: The Defender D300 uses the Ingenium AJ300D — a 3.0-litre inline-six diesel with mild-hybrid assistance. It's been fitted to L663-generation Defenders since 2020 across 90, 110 and 130 body styles.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Land Rover Defender D300 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,800. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Defender D300?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact engine specification before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild Ingenium AJ300D D300 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace timing chain components, injector seals, bearings, gaskets and the DC-DC converter as standard on every AJ300D rebuild. For early production models (2019-2020), we also inspect and replace affected electrical injectors.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Defender D300 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Defender D300 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a Defender D300 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most D300 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
